title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: goal CleanLASA make easy import clean LASA (Longitudinal Aging Study Amsterdam) SPSS data files R. applies correct variable value labels LASA documentation, handles differences waves, flags variables matched documentation can checked manually, helps find open right LASA documentation topic file code.

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: can install development version CleanLASA GitHub :
code: # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("Highmeadows/CleanLASA")

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: main entry point read_lasa_sav(), detects LASA datafile ’re working dispatches correct import/cleaning function automatically: LASA data file handled file-specific apply_lasa[file_code]_labels() function, read_lasa_sav() dispatches automatically. package currently supports: can also called directly, data frame already imported haven::read_sav(), ’d rather skip filename auto-detection read_lasa_sav(): future, similar functions built datafiles.
code: library(CleanLASA)  # Import and label a LASA .sav file  # importing the data should generally be in this fomrat: data <- read_lasa_sav("path/to/LASA[wave][file_code].sav")  # Specific examples: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav") # LASA wave B file 046 data <- read_lasa_sav("LASA_data/LASAZ004.sav") # LASA wave Z file 004 data <- read_lasa_sav("Documents/Research/data/LAS2B011.sav") # LASA wave 2B file 011 data <- read_lasa_sav("lasazoa1.sav") # LASA wave Z file oa1 data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAJFI.sav") # LASA wave J file FI # Specifically for LASA046 (Physical Activity): raw <- haven::read_sav("LASAC046.sav", user_na = TRUE) data <- apply_lasa046_labels(raw, wave = "C")  # wave must be supplied explicitly, since it can't be inferred from data # alone (unlike read_lasa_sav(), which reads it from the file name): data_mb <- apply_lasa046_labels(haven::read_sav("LASMB046.sav"), wave = "MB") data_3b <- apply_lasa046_labels(haven::read_sav("LAS3B046.sav"), wave = "3B")

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: Every apply_lasa*_labels() function – read_lasa_sav(), forwards automatically – accepts five reshaping arguments: name_corrections – manually point canonical suffix (e.g. lphya08) differently-named source column, known typo/renaming data. to_factor – convert categorical variables factors, using SPSS value labels levels. to_numeric – restore count/continuous variables plain numeric, converting negative (missing-reason) codes NA. standardize_names – rename every matched column canonical lowercase LASA name wave code removed (e.g. lphya01), standardize "respnr" (capitalization) "respnr". Always implies split_wavecode = TRUE well. split_wavecode – move wave-letter prefix variable names (e.g. blphya01 becomes lphya01) new "LASA_wave" column, inserted right "respnr" filled file’s wave code (e.g. "B", "2B", "3B"). Regardless arguments, every matched column also keeps original SPSS value coding available reference attributes – attr(x, "original_labels") (codebook) attr(x, "original_values") (raw imported values) – R output can always cross-checked another program’s (e.g. SPSS) coding, even to_numeric/ to_factor reshaping. importing, can check whether variables matched LASA documentation using lasa_label_report(): returns set “faulty” variables — ones couldn’t matched corresponding documentation — can inspect resolve analysis.
code: # Rename columns to their canonical names and split the wave code into its # own column, all in one call: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav", standardize_names = TRUE) names(data)[1:3] #> [1] "respnr"    "LASA_wave" "lphya01"  # split_wavecode also works on its own, without fully standardizing names: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav", split_wavecode = TRUE) lasa_label_report(data)

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: lasa_topics() searches LASA topic overview topics, themes, file codes: table built live LASA website first time ’s needed, cached — rest session disk — doesn’t rebuilt every session. Use refresh = TRUE check live site anything new, newly added wave file code. ’ve found topic file code, lasa_var_info() opens variable-information PDF directly LASA website (PDFs bundled package):
code: # Browse everything lasa_topics()  # Search by topic name (fuzzy matching handles typos and partial names) lasa_topics(topic = "physical act")  # Search by theme or subtheme lasa_topics(theme = "cognitive") lasa_topics(theme = "memory") lasa_var_info("046")               # by file code lasa_var_info("LASA046")           # file code variations are recognized lasa_var_info("Physical activity") # or by topic name lasa_var_info("physical act")      # fuzzy matching handles typos too  # Get the URL without opening it url <- lasa_var_info("046", open = FALSE)

title: Read and label a LASA SPSS data file — read_lasa_sav
text: dispatcher follows LASA filename convention: regular single-letter waves: LASA[wave][file_code].SAV, e.g. LASAE046.SAV; waves 2B, 3B, 4B, MB: LAS[wave][file_code].SAV, e.g. LAS3B046.SAV; information stored across waves: wave code Z, e.g. LASAZ004.SAV; file codes contain 2 3 alphanumeric characters interpreted case-insensitively. File-specific label functions selected convention. file code starts number, expected function apply_lasa[file_code]_labels(); example, file 046 maps apply_lasa046_labels() file 004 maps apply_lasa004_labels(). file code starts letter, expected function apply_lasa_[file_code]_labels(); example, FI maps apply_lasa_fi_labels(). OA files oa1, oa2, oa3 hard-coded family map apply_lasa_oa_labels(). Every apply_*_labels() function package shares parameter contract: data, wave- /file-code-identifying argument, five reshaping arguments documented (name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names, split_wavecode; see apply_lasa046_labels() canonical implementation). read_lasa_sav() declares five reshaping arguments explicitly, defaults shown , callers can discover use without needing know file-specific function ultimately dispatched . selected function must already available package namespace current R session. read_lasa_sav() inspects function's formal arguments (via formals()) : always supplies data; supplies wave /file_code function declares ; supplies name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names, split_wavecode function declares , otherwise warns – rather silently ignoring request – caller supplied non-default value one ; forwards named arguments ... unchanged, file-specific parameters fall outside shared contract. permits shared implementations future apply_lasa_oa_labels(data, file_code, name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names, split_wavecode, ...) coexist wave-aware ones apply_lasa046_labels(data, wave, name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names, split_wavecode). labelling, generic provenance attributes attached: "LASA_wave", "LASA_file_code", "LASA_source_file", "LASA_label_function". File-specific functions attach variable-name matching audit generic "label_report" attribute; retrieve lasa_label_report().

title: Read and label a LASA SPSS data file — read_lasa_sav
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Automatically dispatches to apply_lasa046_labels() dat_e <- read_lasa_sav("LASAE046.SAV")  # Also dispatches to apply_lasa046_labels(), with wave = "3B" dat_3b <- read_lasa_sav("LAS3B046.SAV")  # The four shared reshaping arguments are available directly on # read_lasa_sav(), without needing to know they live on # apply_lasa046_labels() specifically: dat_h <- read_lasa_sav(   "LASAH046.SAV",   to_factor = TRUE,   to_numeric = TRUE,   standardize_names = TRUE )  # split_wavecode = TRUE moves the wave code out of variable names and # into its own "LASA_wave" column, without fully standardizing names: dat_2b <- read_lasa_sav("LAS2B046.SAV", split_wavecode = TRUE)  # Manually correct a mistyped column name: dat_b <- read_lasa_sav(   "LASAB046.SAV",   name_corrections = c(lphya08 = "BLPYA08") )  # Dispatches to apply_lasa004_labels() once that function exists dat_z004 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAZ004.SAV")  # Both dispatch to apply_lasa_oa_labels() once that function exists oa1 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAzoa1.sav") oa2 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAzoa2.sav") } # }
